name: Mesha
overview: Mesha is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Shaharaim according to 1 Chronicles 8:9. Beyond this genealogical note, Scripture does not provide additional details or notable actions associated with him. His mention serves primarily to trace the lineage within the tribe of Benjamin.
namesAndTitles: The name Mesha appears as a proper name in Scripture without a recorded meaning or divine origin. It is simply presented as the personal name of this individual in 1 Chronicles 8:9.
familyAndRelationships: Mesha is recorded as the son of Shaharaim and is also listed as the son of Hodesh in 1 Chronicles 8:9, indicating his place within a specific family line of the tribe of Benjamin. No other family relationships are documented for him in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Mesha's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, which serve to establish the heritage and continuity of God's people. His mention helps preserve the historical and tribal identity important to the biblical narrative, though no further personal deeds or roles are recorded.
